title: Best-iteration reference line treats best_iteration as an array index, misplacing it when loss_history is truncated
description: `bestX` is computed as `xScale(Math.min(Math.max(bestIteration, 0), lossHistory.length - 1))`, but `xScale(i) = marginLeft + (i / (length-1)) * chartW` interprets its argument as a 0-based ARRAY INDEX into `lossHistory`, whereas `result.best_iteration` is the model's actual ITERATION NUMBER. These coincide only when `loss_history` starts at iteration 0 and is 1:1 with its index. The backend (`_train_service.py` `_bounded_loss_history`, default `HAUTE_TRAIN_LOSS_HISTORY_LIMIT=200`) keeps only the last 200 rows (`history[-200:]`) for runs longer than 200 iterations, so the window slides and `lossHistory[0].iteration` is non-zero (e.g. iterations 700..899 for a 900-iteration run). In that case a `best_iteration` of, say, 750 is clamped to `min(750, 199)=199` and the dashed best line is drawn at the far RIGHT edge while the x-axis labels (which correctly render `lossHistory[idx].iteration`) and the legend (`Best iteration (750)`) point elsewhere — a misleading model-diagnostic. The correct placement is to find the array index `j` with `lossHistory[j].iteration === bestIteration` and use `xScale(j)` (and hide the line when no such row is in the visible window).
evidence: Line 76: `const xScale = (i: number) => marginLeft + (i / (lossHistory.length - 1)) * chartW` (i is an index). Line 122-124 x labels use real iterations: `const iter = lossHistory[idx]?.iteration ?? idx`. Line 100: `xScale(Math.min(Math.max(bestIteration, 0), lossHistory.length - 1))` passes an iteration number into the index-based scale. Backend truncation: `_train_service.py` `history = history[-_MAX_TRAIN_LOSS_HISTORY:]` with `_MAX_TRAIN_LOSS_HISTORY = 200`, so index != iteration after truncation; `best_iteration` (schemas.py:840) is the unbounded model best.
